references.text: Gideon was told to send home everyone who was afraid and fearful, just as the law in Deuteronomy prescribed for soldiers who were afraid.
The immediate context where priests and leaders spoke to the people before battle and encouraged them not to fear.
The preceding verses with other reasons for exemption from military service, which form the context for the verse about the fearful man.
Moses urged the people not to be afraid or discouraged, addressing the same theme of courage when facing enemies.
Moses encouraged the people to be strong and courageous, not to fear their enemies, because the Lord goes with them.
Joshua was commanded to be strong and courageous, not afraid, reflecting the same theme of courage in war.
The prophet Isaiah uses similar language about strengthening those who have a fearful heart.
Hebrews warns against shrinking back in fear and encourages faith and perseverance.
